title: DDIA 5 · ENCODING & EVOLUTION
subtitle: Old and new code run side by side, so data must be readable in both directions; and data flows through databases, services, workflows and messages.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.

blocks.text: v1 updates the name and writes the whole object back, and phone is gone. Old code must preserve unknown fields.
Breaking changes: required fields, renumbering tags, or changing a type in an incompatible way.
Messages: the sender doesn't wait. A broker buffers, retries, and fans out. Producer and consumer evolve independently, so a schema registry keeps them compatible.
Each step's result is logged. After a crash the workflow replays: logged steps return their result, so nothing runs twice. Code must be deterministic.

items: A broker buffers, redelivers, and fans out
Queue: one consumer per message; topic: every subscriber
Requests: backward compat; responses: forward compat
"How do you deploy schema changes with zero downtime?"
Expand → migrate → contract: add the nullable column, deploy code that writes both, backfill, switch reads, and only then drop the old column.
"How do Kafka producers and consumers evolve?"
Avro or Protobuf with a schema registry enforcing backward-compatible changes. Consumers upgrade on their own schedule.
gRPC (Protobuf, HTTP/2) for internal high-QPS calls; REST/JSON for public APIs and browsers.
Durable workflow or saga with persisted state, plus idempotency keys on every external call.

blocks.text: "Every message carries a schema version, and we only add optional fields. That lets the booking service deploy without coordinating with its consumers."
